parts.text: Which claim correctly explains both observations?

options.text: Liquid and gas particles keep moving, so they carry colour and fragrance through the water or air.
Spreading happens first and only then do the water or air particles begin to move.
Colour and fragrance spread only if Ira stirs the water or fans the air.
Hotter water spreads the colour more slowly because its particles move less.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Ira places a few potassium permanganate grains in still water and watches the colour spread without stirring. She also notices perfume fragrance filling a room.

part_answers.answer: Constant particle motion mixes colour and fragrance through the liquid or gas; higher temperature speeds the motion and the spreading.

teacher.key_rationale: Particle motion spreads colour and fragrance; hotter water speeds spreading. Reversing cause and effect, requiring stirring, or saying hotter water slows spreading all miss that hinge.
